newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKEY C.BANK CUTS MONEY RATES ON LOWER BOND YIELD.
newsitem.headline: TURKEY C.BANK CUTS MONEY RATES ON LOWER BOND YIELD.

text.p: The Turkish central bank cut its money market rates by between 2-3 points on Wednesday, following a sharp drop in the Treasury's bond auction yield on Tuesday, bankers said.
They said the central bank move was welcomed by the market as it reduced the gap between money and bond market rates.

The central bank lowered its overnight bid-offer rates to 54-74 pct from Tuesday's 56-77, its tomorrow/next rates to 59-69 percent from 62-72 and its tomorrow/week rates to 60-70 percent from the previous 63-73.

"The central bank's move is positive, at least in the short term. Before the rate cut, money market rates were not parallel to the government's forecast of lower inflation in 1997," said a treasury manager of a private bank.
"By lowering its money rates, the central bank also lessened the gap which existed between money and bond market rates," he added.
The Treasury slashed the yield by 13.2 points to 99.24 percent (including 12 percent witholding tax) on its 399-day bond auction on Tuesday, from the previous auction on January 7.
It alloted 200.3 trillion lira of a total 564.2 trillion lira offer, in line with expectations.
T-bill and bond yields were mixed and traded in narrow ranges, after diving by as much as five points on Tuesday due to the auction where strong demand was expected.
Bankers said inflation-plus-risk-premium government papers expected to be issued soon spurred demand for outstanding government securities as well as for February 25, 1998 papers sold in the auction.
They said the market feared that the new risk-premium papers might produce lower returns than the existing ones.

The central bank had last lowered its overnight money bid-offer rates on January 4 to 56-77 percent from 57-78 after lower-than-expected December inflation data and plunging bond market rates due to liquidity and tax news on interest income from government securities.
The lira dived to 114,940 against the dollar, from Tuesday's 114,150 close due to a sharply higher dollar/mark parity and lower money rates.
The Turkish government's wholesale inflation target for 1997 is 57.7 percent, down sharply from 84.9 percent in 1996.
